topics.name: Prepositions of time (at, on, in, for, since)

options: The sun rose at six o'clock.
The sun raised at six o'clock.
The sun risen at six o'clock.
questions.rule: rise - rose is intransitive (no object). raise is transitive: it needs an object.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct preposition.
options: The light reappeared at midnight.
The light reappeared on midnight.
The light reappeared in midnight.
questions.rule: Use at with clock times and midnight, noon, dawn.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: risen
raised
rise

questions.rule: The verb has an object (the cannon), so use the transitive verb raise - raised.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: in
since
at

questions.rule: Use at with clock times: at eight o'clock.

questions.before: When we reached the jetty, the boat
options: has
have
had
questions.rule: The boat left before we reached, so use the past perfect: had left.

options: on
in
at
questions.rule: Use on with days: on Monday, on Monday morning.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a transitive verb.
questions.rule: sharpened is transitive: its object is his harpoon.
on + a day: on a Sunday morning.

chat: What time does the boat leave tomorrow?
options: It leaves on seven o'clock in the morning.
It leaves at seven o'clock in the morning.
It leaves at seven o'clock on the morning.
questions.rule: at + clock time, in the morning: at seven o'clock in the morning.

options: The cannon was loaded by the gunner.
The cannon is loaded by the gunner.
The cannon was load by the gunner.
questions.rule: Simple past active becomes was + past participle: The cannon was loaded.

options: Ned Land lay his harpoon on the deck.
Ned Land lied his harpoon on the deck.
Ned Land laid his harpoon on the deck.
questions.rule: lay - laid is transitive (lay something down). lie - lay has no object.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The animal had disappear before the crew could fire.
The animal has disappeared before the crew could fire.
The animal had disappeared before the crew could fire.
questions.rule: The earlier past action takes the past perfect: had + past participle = had disappeared.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: raised
risen
arose

questions.rule: a loud cheer is an object, so use transitive raise: raised a loud cheer.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: finishing
finished
finishes

questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had already finished.

options: lay
lie
lain
questions.rule: The books are the object, so use transitive lay (put down). lie takes no object.

options: in
on
at
questions.rule: Use in with months, seasons and years: in June.
Past perfect: had + past participle: had cleared.

chat: Did you see the sun rise this morning?
options: Yes, it raised over the sea at six.
Yes, it rose over the sea at six.
Yes, it rised over the sea at six.
questions.rule: The sun rises by itself (no object). Past of rise is rose.

chat: What did the coach tell you?
options: He said me that the match would start at four.
He said that the match will starts at four.
He said that the match would start at four.
questions.rule: said that (no object after said), and will becomes would: would start.

options: Ned said that I saw a whale.
Ned said that he seen a whale.
Ned said that he saw a whale.
questions.rule: I becomes he, and the simple present see moves back to the simple past saw.

options: The light disappeared near midnight.
The light was disappeared near midnight.
The light disappear near midnight.
questions.rule: disappear is intransitive, so it cannot be passive: The light disappeared.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct preposition.
options: The chase had gone on since an hour.
The chase had gone on for an hour.
The chase had gone on from an hour.
questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (an hour) and since with a starting point (since dawn).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: missing
missed
misses

questions.rule: The earlier action is past perfect: had + past participle = had missed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: spoke
talked
said

questions.rule: told needs a person after it (told us). With no person, use said: The captain said the storm was coming closer.

questions.after: know what kind of creature it was.
options: not
did not
do not
questions.rule: After said, the present does not know moves back to the past: did not know. A negative verb needs a helper.

options: rose
raised
rised
questions.rule: There is no object, so use intransitive rise. Its past is rose.
Reported speech: said that + subject + backshifted verb (can becomes could).

chat: Did you catch the 8 a.m. bus?
options: No, it had already left when I reached the stop.
No, it has already left when I reached the stop.
No, it had already leave when I reached the stop.
questions.rule: The bus left before I reached, so use the past perfect: had already left.

options: The harpoon was launched by Ned Land.
The harpoon was launch by Ned Land.
The harpoon launched by Ned Land.
questions.rule: Simple past passive: was + past participle: was launched.

questions.source: The crew loaded the guns. Then they waited for dawn.
options: After the crew had load the guns, they waited for dawn.
After the crew had loaded the guns, they waited for dawn.
After the crew has loaded the guns, they waited for dawn.
questions.rule: The first action takes the past perfect: After the crew had loaded ..., then the simple past.

options: Was the shell fire by the old gunner?
Was the shell fired by the old gunner?
Did the shell fired by the old gunner?
questions.rule: Passive question: Was + subject + past participle: Was the shell fired ...?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: The monster had vanished by dawn, hadn't it?
The monster had vanished by dawn, didn't it?
The monster had vanished by dawn, had it?
questions.rule: A positive sentence with had takes the negative tag hadn't it?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: at
by
for

questions.rule: many years is a length of time, so use for: for many years.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: shook
shaking
shaken

questions.rule: Passive: were + past participle. The past participle of shake is shaken.

questions.after: away before the cannon was fired.
options: has swum
had swam
had swum
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle. swim - swam - swum, so had swum.
Passive: object + was + past participle + by + doer: was thrown by Ned Land.

chat: How long have you lived in Ratnagiri?
options: We have lived here since six years.
We have lived here for six years.
We are living here for six years.
questions.rule: How long asks for the present perfect + for a length of time: have lived here for six years.

chat: What did the guide ask you at the aquarium?
options: He asked whether I had ever seen a whale.
He asked whether had I ever seen a whale.
He asked whether I have ever saw a whale.
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order: whether I had ever seen.

questions.source: The Commander said, "We will wait for daylight."
options: The Commander said that we will wait for daylight.
The Commander said that they will waited for daylight.
The Commander said that they would wait for daylight.
questions.rule: We becomes they, and will becomes would: they would wait.

questions.source: The order was given by the Commander.
options: The Commander given the order.
The Commander gives the order.
The Commander gave the order.
questions.rule: was given is simple past passive, so the active is simple past: The Commander gave the order.

options: Aronnax said me that he had never seen such a fast creature before.
Aronnax said that he had never saw such a fast creature before.
Aronnax said that he had never seen such a fast creature before.
questions.rule: said that (no object), and past perfect needs the past participle: had never seen.

options: Exhausted after the chase, the sailors laid on the deck until dawn.
Exhausted after the chase, the sailors lay on the deck until dawn.
Exhausted after the chase, the sailors lain on the deck until dawn.
questions.rule: The sailors rested with no object, so use lie. Its past is lay. laid needs an object.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: from
for
at

questions.rule: twenty hours is a length of time, so use for: No one had slept for twenty hours.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: fixing
fixed
fixes

questions.rule: had been + past participle (past perfect passive): had been fixed.

questions.after: his arm and hurled the harpoon with all his strength.
options: raised
rose
risen
questions.rule: his arm is an object, so use transitive raise - raised, matching hurled.
By + a past time often takes the past perfect: had rolled away.

chat: What did Ned Land tell the Commander?
options: He told him that there was definitely a whale in their waters.
He told to him that there was definitely a whale in their waters.
He told him that there were definitely a whale in their waters.
questions.rule: told him (no to), and a whale is singular: there was.

chat: Has the old ship been repaired yet?
options: Yes, it has repaired and painted too.
Yes, it has been repaired and painted too.
Yes, it has been repair and painted too.
questions.rule: The ship does not repair itself, so use the passive: has been repaired.

questions.source: Ned Land said, "There is a whale lurking in our waters."
options: Ned Land said that there were a whale lurking in their waters.
Ned Land said that there is a whale lurking in our waters.
Ned Land said that there was a whale lurking in their waters.
questions.rule: is becomes was and our becomes their: there was a whale ... in their waters.

questions.source: The crew greeted the order with three cheers.
options: The order was greeted by the crew with three cheers.
The order is greeted by the crew with three cheers.
The order was greet by the crew with three cheers.
questions.rule: Simple past active becomes was + past participle: The order was greeted by the crew.
